main_chase_cards.name: Bellossom
main_chase_cards.why: Bellossom makes the Information Pack route feel gentle rather than obscure. It is a free shop-counter insert with a bright Kimura illustration and a card text about flowers making pleasant sound when Bellossom dances. The card's charm is that the route itself is humble, but the object still feels cared for.

key_artists.name: Naoyo Kimura
examples: Neo Premium File 2 Eevee / Espeon / Umbreon
key_artists.why: Kimura is one of the artists who made Pokemon feel like printed storybook space, not just battle data. Bellossom fits that lane: a floral, dancing Pokemon carried by a plain information packet, made collectible by a soft image and a very specific paper route.

claims.text: The local catalog and Bulbapedia align on April 1, 2001 for Pokemon Card Information Vol. 2 Bellossom distribution.
Bulbapedia states the Bellossom promo was available in Japan in the second volume of Pokemon Card Information and distributed for free at participating stores from April 1, 2001.
The local release family models one row: Bellossom source index 233, with the promotion note Pokemon Card Information Vol. 2 insert.

Bulbapedia's 2001 unnumbered-promo table places Bellossom after the Vol. 1 Dunsparce route and before Vol. 3 Pryce's Lapras, making it the middle step of the early Information Pack sequence modeled in this queue.

Bulbapedia identifies Naoyo Kimura / 木村直代 as a Pokemon TCG illustrator notable for Neo Series and Southern Islands work, as well as Pokemon Tales picture books and later Pokemon x Van Gogh collaboration artwork.

Pokemon Card Information Vol. 2 matters because the Information Pack route turns an ordinary store handout into a preserved collector object; Bellossom's dance-and-flower identity makes that route feel especially tender.
This release dossier carries a special identification packet for Pokemon Card Information Vol. 2 Bellossom source index 233.

narrative.human_title: Pokemon Card Information Vol. 2 — Bellossom as the soft middle of the shop-counter sequence
narrative.why_it_matters: Vol. 2 gives the Information Pack route its gentlest face. Dunsparce made the route charmingly odd; Bellossom makes it floral, rhythmic, and quietly collectible. A free participating-store handout becomes a small paper vessel for Naoyo Kimura's Neo-era softness, a Bellossom dance, and the strange fact that even an information sheet could carry real TCG memory.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Bellossom as source index 233 in the Pokemon Card Information Vol. 2 unnumbered-promo source row.
Bulbapedia identifies the card as Bellossom / キレイハナ Kireihana, a Grass-type Stage 2 Pokemon card evolving from Gloom, with HP 80 and No. 182.
Bulbapedia lists Floral Spin / フローラルスピン as the card's attack, with Fire weakness and two retreat cost.
Bulbapedia identifies Naoyo Kimura / 木村直代 as the illustrator for the Bellossom Information Pack promo.
Bulbapedia records the bottom-border text as Information Pack bonus card part 2, making the route itself a visible card-detail clue.
Bulbapedia states the card's Pokedex entry comes from Pokemon Silver; the entry describes Bellossom living in southern lands and making pleasant sounds when its petals touch while dancing.

Naoyo Kimura's broader work includes Neo Series cards, Southern Islands, Pokemon Tales picture books, and later Pokemon x Van Gogh collaboration artwork, which makes Bellossom part of a much larger printed-storybook visual lane.

Bulbapedia's TCG Pocket Bellossom page notes that a later TCG Pocket illustration reused artwork first featured on the Japan-only Bellossom Information Pack promo; this is a later reuse signal, not original-route proof.
not_claiming: that TCG Pocket creates the original 2001 route

narrative.human_title: Bellossom — source index 233, the little flower dance in the packet
narrative.why_it_matters: Bellossom is the kind of card that makes the catalog feel alive. It is not trying to roar. It is a free store-packet promo illustrated by Naoyo Kimura, with Floral Spin, Silver-era petal music, and border text that tells you exactly how it entered the world. Later reuse of the image only underlines what collectors already feel: this quiet 2001 handout carried an image good enough to keep traveling.
